<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19097>

Paul Murrell (<mailto:paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz|paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz>) changed:

           What    |Removed                     |Added
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
             Status|UNCONFIRMED                 |CONFIRMED
     Ever confirmed|0                           |1
                 CC|                            |paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz

--- Comment #1 from Paul Murrell (<mailto:paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz|paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz>) ---
I can confirm this on Linux at least.

And the patch resolves the segfault (on Linux).

I wonder whether there is anything in common with the fix that was made for
segfaults from closing devices during graphics drawing (commit 88805), in which
case, whether this fix could/should make use of the device "lock" mechanism
introduced by that fix.  

This might benefit from input from someone with more expertise in event
handling.

Also, in the patch, the `break` that happens if the device is NOT alive could
perhaps be accompanied by a warning that an attempt to close the device is
being ignored (c.f. commit 88805).
